$comment: The app's key screens, captured from each platform's preview build: the iPhone's (#331) and Android's (#372). Each screen opens by deep link (sdachurchapp://<path>) after its settings are saved; each variant adds the settings listed under variants. A variant that changes one platform's own settings (iosTextSize on the iPhone; fontScale and displayScale on Android) is taken only there, and a screen with platforms only on those. Screenshots are named <platform>/<screen>-<variant>.png. checks lists automatic image checks for a screen, mustShowLines regular expressions that some line of its text must match (or { line, minLeft } for a line that must also start at least minLeft of the way across, such as right-aligned text), mustNotShowLines ones that no line may match, variantRules more of either for one variant (a rule written { line, platforms } applies on those platforms only, such as a line the Android phone's smaller screen leaves below the fold), and tabs false for a screen without the tab bar, such as the Bible while reading (scripts/check-screens.cjs); appStore lists, per App Store language, the iPhone shots to upload, in order, appStoreIpad the iPad's, from the screens that list ipadVariants (#324), googlePlay, per Google Play language, the Android ones (at most 8), and googlePlayTablet the Android tablet's, from the screens that list androidTabletVariants (#695), which a later language's tablet set can join. Each screen's group names the related screens it is captured with, on one of up to five runners at once (#453): put a new screen in the group for its part of the app, as groups describes. A test fails if a group would take more than 8 minutes on the iPhone, or 7 on the iPad. That limit is a reminder to prune, not a rule: first drop variants that repeat what another shot already shows and screens no longer worth a check, spend the time saved on screens and states no shot covers yet (#456), then move some related screens to a lighter group or split one, and if a group is still over after that, raise the limit. Leave out screens that show members' names or photos, such as the bulletin, the team page, the fellowship page, and the worship schedule. A path's popup= opens one of that screen's popups or dialogs, in the preview build only (#372); its shot skips the tab and verse-button checks, which the popup covers or dims. The Bible's play=1 starts its audio the same way (#551). A screen's record names what the app saves of such an action, which scripts/key-screen-records.cjs checks, saying when the network was the cause of a failure; later takes a second screenshot that many seconds after the first, <platform>/<screen>-<variant>-later.png; and mustAdvance is a regular expression for a time, its first two groups the minutes and seconds, that must have moved on in the later shot by at least half that time. Every download a reviewer opens stays under the 50 MB Chrome looks inside, with no app in it: Chrome blocked the one download that held the screenshots and the unsigned app (#484), and called 1.7.0's 349 MB of iPhone and iPad shots dangerous. scripts/pack-review-downloads.cjs packs each device's shots as palette PNGs, in parts if need be, and fails the join if they'd need more parts than the workflow uploads ("Downloads under 50 MB" in docs/operations/native-builds.md).

ipad.$comment: The iPad (#324): the 13-inch iPad Pro, whose screen is the size App Store Connect's iPad screenshots take. Only the screens that list ipadVariants are taken on it, on a runner of its own; its variants can turn it to landscape (orientation), which serve-sim does, since simctl can't. See "iPad key screens" in docs/operations/native-builds.md.

android.$comment: The emulator. phone is the best-selling Android phone of Q1 2026, the Samsung Galaxy A07 4G (Counterpoint), sold mostly in the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America, where most Adventists live: a 6.7-inch 720 × 1600 screen at 300 dpi, 384 × 853 dp. The US's best-selling Androids, the Galaxy A16 and A17, are 384 dp wide too, as this church's members' phones are likely to be. Google Play takes no screenshot taller than 2:1, so its shots are taken on a second emulator of googlePlay's size. tablet is a 10-inch tablet held upright (#695), 800 dp wide as the Pixel Tablet and other 10-inch tablets at 1280 × 800 dp are, but 9:16 rather than their 16:10, the shape Google Play's tablet screenshots take: 1620 × 2880 at 324 dpi, 800 × 1422 dp. The app's tablet layout follows the screen's width and its shorter side, not its height, so it lays out as on a real tablet, with a little more of each page in view, and the one emulator takes both the tablet's checks and its Google Play shots. google_apis, not google_apis_playstore, because the capture writes the app's settings as root. See "Android key screens" in docs/operations/native-builds.md.

splitWindows.$comment: The iPad's Split View and Slide Over windows, in points (dp at 2x, 320 dpi), taken on their own emulators (#324): Slide Over, and the 11-inch iPad's half, the 13-inch iPad's half in portrait, and its two-thirds in landscape.

groups.home: The Home tab and the pages it opens, other than the hymnals: Discover, About, and Give, and first-launch setup over it.
groups.bible-reading: The Bible reader's layout: one and two translations, the header and its back arrow, text scrolled under the status bar, the popup a tapped verse opens, and Offline Bible Audio, which its audio settings open, with its narrator popup.
groups.bible-text: What the Bible reader shows: Chinese, Cantonese, Simplified Chinese, pinyin, and Spanish text, long chapters, and Selah.
groups.library: The Explore tab, Sabbath School, and the Library: featured books, shelves, and each collection. Also, on the iPhone only, a children's lesson open in Quick Look (#551). Sabbath School moved here from worship-and-you in 1.7.0, whose release run took 37 minutes on that group, with the iPad's shots, against 24 on this one.
groups.worship-and-you: The hymnals and the You tab with its open-source licenses page and its Text size and Language dialogs. Also, on the iPhone only, Bible audio playing (#551).

screens.name: setup
screens.$comment: First-launch setup, which shows until has-completed-setup is saved: its first step of five (#523, #669), the welcome and the language, full screen from 1.7.2 (#681), each language a card with a picture of the tab bar in it, and the step dots and Next at the bottom, below the scrolling part, so the way on stays in view. RapidOCR reads the white Next on its blue button as Net at the Android phone's default size, so there only the large variant requires it.

screens.name: home
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text: the app at 200% with the iPhone's accessibility-large text (2×), held to 3.2× by the combined cap, as with Android's largest font at 200%, where the tab labels used to wrap (#380); xl-android-font-max and es-xl-android-font-max are that case itself, with the same rules, except that the Android phone's narrower screen may wrap the heading between its words; and android-display-large is Android's largest display size. Their verse-card buttons and heading must show whole words, not “Shar” or “Versícul / o” (#385). The verse changes daily, and a long one, such as John 1:1 or Genesis 1:27 in English or most verses in Spanish, pushes one button or both below the shot, so no rule requires a button. English instead requires its heading whole on one line and fails on a line ending in a cut-off button word, such as “Shar” or “Rea”; Spanish requires its heading, with or without the accent, which OCR can miss when the photo's cross runs behind it. The tab-label check fails on a wrapped label, or one pushed up out of the tab bar's area by an overgrown bar. Not the iPhone's very largest size: at about 6× in all, page titles break mid-word, which isn't a useful baseline. es-large is Spanish at 150% on the phones: on the Android phone's 384 points, "Compartir" didn't fit beside Leer Versículo and broke mid-word, so the buttons stack wherever a word wouldn't fit (#324). The Sabbath countdown is three lines, with no date (#593): "Sabbath starts in" (or "Happy Sabbath!" during the Sabbath), the timer on a line of its own, and the place. default, es-large, zh and zh-cn require the label whole and the timer, and fail on a date line. The timer's rule allows up to three characters before it, for the days: Vision can read the iPhone's Courier "1d" as "ld" or "la", and RapidOCR can drop the space after it, as it dropped the one before "in" on the Android tablet (#695). The check of Chinese dates written out by hand moved to sabbath-school's zh shot.

mustShowLines: ^(距離安息日還有|安息日快樂！?)$
^(距离安息日还有|安息日快乐！?)$

screens.name: bible-dual
screens.$comment: The header's translation button in full: each translation's language badge and name, EN BSB + 繁 CUV, not cut to B… or C… (#376). From 1.7.0 it has no 文A icon, whose readings (XA, JA, 文A) these rules used to need; the bigger badges say the same. Vision has read the 繁 badge as "*", so only EN is required, and RapidOCR has read CUV's gold C on standard contrast's dark brown as "c", so either case passes. On the iPad, Vision can read the book button's chevron as part of its name, "Psalmsv". In the iPad's 320-point Slide Over window (w320, on Android), the book's pill showed only "…" beside 23 and Vs. (#681): it must name the book, in full or as "Ps".

screens.name: bible-dual-back
screens.$comment: Opened from Home, so the header also has a back arrow and less room. When it's tight, the translation button gives up its names, cut short and then dropped, and only then takes a row of its own (#376). Both full names fit at 100% everywhere, and on the iPhone at 150% and 200% too, since dropping the 文A icon (1.7.0) saved more room than the bigger badges took. The Android phone's narrower screen drops them at 150% and 200%, leaving EN + 繁, so there only the badge is required.

screens.name: bible-cuv
screens.$comment: Mandarin is the default narrator, so the audio button shows 國語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-cantonese
screens.$comment: With the Cantonese narrator chosen, the audio button shows 粵語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-after-spanish
screens.$comment: The Spanish Bible was open with the CUV underneath, then a link opens the CUV. Its book names must replace the Spanish ones, which once stayed until a restart (#373). The interface is English, as when the bug showed, so Vision reads the dock in English first and misses 詩篇; it reads a stale Salmos reliably.

screens.name: bible-cuvs
screens.$comment: Simplified characters, so the audio button shows 国语.

screens.name: bible-scrolled
screens.$comment: Opens at John 3:14, so earlier verses sit under the status bar; checks it stays clear. In the iPad's 320-point Slide Over window (w320, on Android), the book's pill must name John, not show only "…" (#681).

screens.name: bible-verse-popup
screens.$comment: The popup a tapped verse opens, opened by popup=verse in the preview build (#372): the reference as its title beside an X, with no Close button (#464). A popup covers or dims the tab bar and chapter controls, so those aren't checked. The original-language Greek ships with the app, so its credit must show, with the license CC BY 4.0 requires (it may wrap onto its own line). Vision reads the share icon before Share Verse as <.

screens.name: bible-search
screens.$comment: Whole-Bible search (#516), opened by search= in the key-screens build, as the capture can't type. Genesis 22 is open, so its match for Moriah comes first, then the whole Bible's two by book, with counts. OCR may read the · between a heading and its count as another mark, so the rules allow any, and a result's quote icon as • or 66 before its reference. The results are a page of their own, over the reader's Verse button and the tab bar, which used to show through them.

screens.name: bible-audio-settings
screens.$comment: The audio settings popup, opened by popup=audio-settings in the preview build (#372): its title beside an X (#464), and the CUV's two audio languages, in English (the Google Play screenshot) and Chinese. The audio button behind it shows 國語, so the rules require lines only the popup shows. Vision misses the lone 粵語 label, so the Cantonese row is found by its credit, WordProject. It's centred like the other popups: until 1.3.2 it sat at the bottom, its title 47% of the way down where theirs are at 25 to 32%, so the title must be no farther down than 40%. Under the audio languages, Listen offline is one row that opens Offline Bible Audio in the You tab, where Bible audio is downloaded and deleted (#556); it must show, though the Android phone's shorter popup may leave the row below the fold.

screens.name: offline-bible-audio
screens.$comment: Offline Bible Audio, where Bible audio is downloaded and deleted (#556), as the Bible's audio settings open it for Souer's English narration: the narrator, named language first (the user: people don't know who Souer is), then the whole Bible, the Old Testament, and its sections, closed, each with its book count and size. A key-screen build has nothing downloaded, so no row offers delete. Below the narrator, Download notifications (#610), the switch for the app's own download notifications, which both phones that capture have. The text readers may read a closed section's chevron with its title ("> Law") and drop the spaces in "英語 – Souer" and "66 卷", so the rules allow both. RapidOCR on Android can read the narrator line's dash in Chinese as a full-width －, and "66 books" without its space.

screens.name: bible-audio-mobile-data
screens.$comment: The question Offline Bible Audio asks before a download on mobile data (#611), by popup=mobile-data in the preview build, for Souer's whole Bible: the app's own popup, not the system's alert, with its answers as stacked buttons, Use mobile data first and Cancel last, and no X. In Spanish at the largest text sizes, the title and the longest answer may wrap, on the iPhone a word to a line, but no answer may be cut short with an ellipsis, as Paper's one-line Button cut "Usar datos m..." (run 41714586130), and Cancelar must show in the popup: at the iPhone's largest, the title and answers once overflowed it, and Cancelar showed over the page below (run 41741902378). The title scrolls with the message now, above the answers. The text readers may read the curly apostrophe in "You’re" as a straight one, and drop the hyphen in "Wi-Fi".

screens.name: bible-audio-notifications-question
screens.$comment: The app's own question before the phone's, the first time a long download starts (#610), by popup=notifications in the preview build: what the notifications are for, that the download keeps going either way, and where to turn them off, with Allow first and Not now. iOS asks only for a word when it's done, so its words are shorter. The text readers may read the curly apostrophes as straight ones, and the Chinese message wraps inside 下載都會繼續 on the Android phone, so the rule checks 不論是否允許.

screens.name: offline-bible-audio-narrator
screens.$comment: Offline Bible Audio's narrator popup, which lists every narrator to download with what's on the phone, by popup=narrator in the preview build (#324). A key-screen build has nothing downloaded. Its iPad shot checks the popup's width: when it was new, it had a percentage width, which on iOS fills 90% of an iPad. In the bible-text group, the compiling runner's, since the bible-reading group's phones are at their time limit.

screens.name: bible-audio-download-tip
screens.$comment: The audio settings popup as the marked audio button opens it when playback keeps stopping to load (#595), by popup=audio-download-tip in the preview build. The BSB has four narrators above Listen offline, so the popup scrolls down to it: the tip's line, and the Offline Bible Audio row below it, which opens the downloads (#556), must show. The line doesn't say "keeps stopping", which Android's check reserves for the system's crash dialog. On the iPad, the dimmed page shows beside the popup, and Vision can read its words into the tip's line, so the rule finds the tip anywhere in a line. Vision once missed the Offline Bible Audio row's title there while reading the line below it (run 41836240862), so either line of the row shows it.
mustShowLines: ^(Offline Bible Audio|Download a book, a section, or the whole Bible)$

screens.name: bible-long-chapter
screens.$comment: Psalm 119 from verse 100, for three-digit verse numbers at large text sizes. RapidOCR may read a verse number without the space after it, as 102I, so the rules only require no further digit.

screens.name: bible-higgaion-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:16 in the BSB ends with "Higgaion Selah", plain text after the verse's poetry lines in the HelloAO data. At the default text size the reader shows it right-aligned under the verse, so it must start in the right half of the screen.

screens.name: bible-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:20 in the BSB ends with "Selah" alone, right-aligned on its own line, so it must start in the right half of the screen. The rule needs a line starting with Selah, so 9:16's "Higgaion Selah" can't satisfy it.

screens.name: explore
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text check the tab labels at about 4× text, as on Home (#380), and their Android counterparts at Android's largest font. xl-android-font-max is also the Android counterpart of max. max is the app at 200% with the iPhone's very largest text, about 6× before the combined cap (MAX_COMBINED_TEXT_SCALE) held it to 3.2×; at 6× the Library card's title read "Libr". In Chinese the Library is 精選書庫 (hand-picked library), and the In-depth Bible Study card for the SDA Bible app shows below Spotify; it's Chinese only, since the app's commentary and nearly all its books are Chinese (#554).

screens.name: library
screens.$comment: The featured carousel's arrows sit beside its dots, under the carousel, so they never cover its first book's title (#447): The Bruised Reed in every language, whole on one line, right of the cover. The shelf below wraps the same title after The Bruised, so only the carousel's line matches. Vision isn't asked to read the arrows: a chevron alone in a circle is no reliable text. Each shelf's row scrolls sideways past the content column to the screen's edge on purpose, so a shelf longer than the column, such as the Chinese Christian Classics' six, shows a cover cut off at the edge: wideContent skips the iPad's column and edge checks (#681).

screens.name: library-contemporary
screens.$comment: Chinese readers get a shelf of today's Adventist writers, books the church's leaders chose from the Chinese Union Mission's reader, titled in the app's script; the covers are the reader's, in Simplified. The Traditional shelf title and 地上的最後一夜 (最后 on its cover) can only come from the app's own text (#554). The second row's titles are below the fold on both phones.

screens.name: library-children
screens.$comment: Books by other writers lead the Children shelf, and Ellen G. White's books for adults stay on her own shelf (#391).

screens.name: library-youth
screens.$comment: Pastor Hsi leads the Youth shelf, ahead of Ellen G. White's books, and The Pilgrim's Progress follows in each reader's language: its 1869 Mandarin edition for Chinese readers, and Chapel Library's for Spanish (#391). Its English and Spanish titles wrap, differently on each phone, so only their first words are checked.

screens.name: sabbath-school
screens.$comment: The adult lessons with this week's mission video between them (#508), in each language. The card's description names a different Sabbath each week, so only its title is checked, by its first words, since the Android phone wraps the Spanish one. In Chinese the title is 本週聖工剪影, or the Sabbath of the last Mandarin video the phone found, such as 10月31日聖工剪影; and the video's line starts with its Sabbath's date, such as 11月7日安息日, whether it's the Mandarin video or the English page. That date is the key screens' check of Chinese dates written out by hand (formatAppDate): on Android, Hermes once showed the Simplified one in English ("Friday, November 6"). The card pushes the first children's age group, checked here before (#338), below the fold on the iPhone too.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-download
screens.$comment: The popup a tap on a children's lesson opens while its PDF downloads (#529). Key screens can't tap, so a key-screens build opens it from popup=, with a fixed 5.1 of 14.2 MB. The iPhone's text recognition reads "14.2MB", without the space.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-offline
screens.$comment: The same popup offline with no copy of the lesson (#529, part of #533): it says so, with only the X, in Chinese.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-viewer
screens.$comment: A children's lesson downloaded and open in Quick Look, the iPhone's own viewer (#529, #551). popup=lesson-viewer opens the Beginner student lesson in a key-screens build as a tap would: this week's PDF is about 1 MB. The app records how it opened (record), and the capture fails unless Quick Look opened, saying whether the network was the cause. Where the week's lesson has no PDF yet, the browser opens its website instead and the run only warns, so the rules accept that page's address too. Nothing of the page beneath may show.

screens.name: bible-audio-playing
screens.$comment: Bible audio playing on the iPhone (#551), which nothing else checks before release: Android's is checked by android-audio-e2e.yml. play=1 starts Psalm 23's Mandarin recording in a key-screens build as a tap on Play would. A second screenshot is taken later seconds after the first, and the elapsed time left of the timeline must have moved on by at least half that (mustAdvance). The player's own status is recorded too (record): if it didn't play, the capture says whether this runner could reach the audio's hosts, so a network failure reads as one. The lock screen's 10- and 30-second skips can't be pressed in the Simulator; test/bible-audio-service.test.ts checks what the app passes them.

screens.name: hymnal-selection
screens.$comment: The hymnal page (#413): a carousel of the hymnals, the app language's first, then the picked hymnal's search and its hymns, each 1985 or 505 hymn with the other hymnal's number, a verse chip beside it (an English hymn's own, and a 505 hymn's 1985 equivalent's in Chinese, such as 詩篇 100 on 505's 1), and the 1985 and 505 hymns' Piano only videos (#424). Vision reads the 文A icon in a chip as XA and a row's treble clef as a character, so those lines are matched anywhere.

screens.name: hymnal
screens.$comment: A link to one hymn, as from the bulletin: the hymnal page opens on the SDA Hymnal with just that hymn, marked, its Chinese 505 number, its With singing and Piano only videos (#424), and Show all hymns. At the app's 200% text size the Chinese 505 · 16 chip must still show its whole number (a long label wraps inside the chip), and the buttons stack, so they and Show all hymns may fall below the shot. The hymnal's name and the hymn's title wrap at 200% too, so there only their first words are required.

screens.name: hymnal-chinese
screens.$comment: An older hymnal route with an old search, highlight=平安夜, opens the hymnal page with that hymnal picked: the 506, not the 505 a Chinese interface would show first, its cover photo cropped to the carousel's 2:3 frame. Its one match, 82, comes first, with its recording labeled 演唱 (With singing) although the 506 has no piano videos yet, then the heading over the matches in the other hymnals, each under its hymnal's name, the 505's 66 first (on the phones: in the iPad's landscape shot, at 150%, it's below the fold), and no longer the hymnal's short name on each result's own line ("505", "1985", "707 新編簡譜"). Vision may read "82. 平安夜" without the space, may read the dash in a hymnal's name as 一, and reads the YouTube logo before 演唱 as a character.

screens.name: discover
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text: the app at 200% with the iPhone's accessibility-large text, held to 3.2× by the combined cap. The two-column cards' titles stay at the default 1.25× (#387), so "About Denomination" must keep "Denomination" whole instead of breaking it as "Den / omination". xl-android-font-max is the same case on Android, at its largest font. es-default-text is Spanish at the app's default 125%: on the Android phone's 384 points, "Compañerismo" was wider than its card's title, so each card shrinks its grid's text just enough to keep the widest word whole (#324). Its ñ may read as another letter.

screens.name: give
screens.$comment: Zelle stays hidden until its address is ready (#392). When shown, its heading sits just above the tab bar.

screens.name: give-daf-sponsors
screens.$comment: In the bible-text group, the lightest, so the home group stays within its time. The Tithe & Offering page's Other Sponsors popup, opened by popup=daf-sponsors (#646). The page's Donor-Advised Fund card, far below the give shot's fold, has a Fidelity Charitable button, which opens a grant to the church, and Other Sponsors, which opens this: an X beside its title and no Close button, the other sponsors the card names, each opening its website, DAFgiving360 saying it was Schwab Charitable, then the church's legal name and EIN for the grant. Each row's open-in-new icon may be read on the end of a line, so lines aren't anchored at their end, and RapidOCR may drop the space after EIN or read its hyphen as a dash.

screens.name: you
screens.$comment: The settings: Contrast, with the choice it reads, high contrast unless a member changed it (#669), and Offline Bible Audio, the last, which lists the Bible audio downloaded for listening offline (#556); the web has none. Since 1.7.0 added Contrast, About & Support's items, Share the App (#555) and Help & Feedback (#541), sit below the tab bar on every phone, so they aren't required here; share-app checks its popup. The Android tablet saves no text size, so Text size must read 150%, the size a tablet starts at (#695).

screens.name: share-app
screens.$comment: The Share the App popup, opened by popup=share-app (#555): an X beside its title, the download page's QR code on white so it scans in the dark theme too, the address, and Share Link, with no Close button. The QR image has no text, so the rules require the address and the button. The button's share icon reads as "<" before its label, so the label isn't anchored at the start.

screens.name: text-size
screens.$comment: The Text size dialog, opened by popup=text-size (#372): an X beside its title, and Reset the only button at its foot, with no Apply, since a size takes effect as it changes (#464). At 200% its text runs past the popups' height limit (POPUP_MAX_HEIGHT_FRACTION in styles/PopupStyles.ts), so the dialog stops there and its text scrolls, leaving room around it to tap. Its title is also on the You screen behind it, so the rules require lines only the dialog shows. The iPad saves no text size, so its shot shows the size a tablet starts at, 150%, and Reset returns there (#324).

You → Contrast (#669): light mode and dark mode, each with high contrast, the default, and standard, with a picture of the tab bar in each. A setting, not a question, so it has an X, which Vision doesn't read as a word. Dark mode is below the fold on a phone.
screens.name: contrast

screens.$comment: First-launch setup's other steps, which a key-screens build opens by the saved setupStep since the capture can't tap Next (#669), so each step has its shot: hard to reach by hand. The text size step, with its sample verse at the chosen size, and Back and Next.
screens.name: setup-text-size

screens.$comment: Setup's appearance step: the four themes, each a card with a picture of the page and tab bar in it (#681), one a row, so Dark sits below the fold on a phone. Each choice's icon can be read into its label, as a colon by RapidOCR or as letters by Vision ("Lo System", "ội Light"), so the labels are anchored only at their end.
screens.name: setup-appearance

screens.$comment: Setup's contrast for light mode (#669): the pictures of high contrast, chosen, and standard, in the light theme, with Next. Titles wrap differently by device, so the rules need only their start, and fail on the other mode's wording.
screens.name: setup-contrast-light

screens.$comment: Setup's last step (#669): the contrast for dark mode, with its pictures in the dark theme, and Get Started. Vision reads the white Get Started on its blue button; RapidOCR may not, so Android doesn't require it.
screens.name: setup-contrast-dark

screens.$comment: The contrast question after an update (#669): shown once, on the first launch after updating, to members who set up an earlier version, which a missing whatsNewSeen stands for. Light mode first, then dark mode (whatsNewStep dark), each with its two pictures, high contrast first, and no other text. From #708 it's setup's own full screen and contrast step, not a popup, so both pictures and the buttons show without a scroll: Standard is required again. A tap on a picture only chooses it, and setup's buttons go on: Next on the first page, Back and Done on the second. Both readers read the words on them, unlike setup's full-width Next on the Android phone, except that RapidOCR read the outlined 上一步 as 步 alone on the Android phone, so only the iPhone and iPad require it. It asks a question, so it has no X.
screens.name: whats-new

screens.$comment: The question's second page: dark mode.
screens.name: whats-new-dark
language
screens.$comment: The Language dialog, opened by popup=language (#372): an X beside its title and no Close button (#464), and each language a card with a picture of the tab bar in it (#681). Its title is also on the You screen behind it, so the rules require an option's description, which only the dialog shows. The pictures leave Simplified Chinese below the fold on a phone.

screens.name: theme
screens.$comment: The Theme dialog, opened by popup=theme: each theme a card with a picture of a page and its tab bar in it, light and dark side by side for System and Sunrise/Sunset (#681), with an X beside its title.
